evidence.summary: s->a=1,s->b=2,b->a=-2 makes a finalize at 1 although its shortest distance is 0.
n=1,a=[5],x=4 is legal and has no answer, but the code outputs 5.
[1,1] is reported as length 2; strict LIS length is 1. lower_bound is required.
Level d costs Theta(n(log n-d)); summing over log n levels gives Theta(n log^2 n).
Weights 0/1 are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finalization is valid; at most O(E) successful lazy pushes use a heap of O(E) size.
One item (w=1,v=1), capacity 2 is used twice by ascending updates, yielding 2 instead of 1.
At a star center, deg=n-1 exclusions each scan n-2 children, so work is Theta(n^2), not O(n log n).
The second test inherits ans; 50000*50000 exceeds signed 32-bit before assignment to long long.
x=-1 satisfies x^2=1 but not x=1, so only the forward implication was shown.
Starting from 0, add 2 then assign 4 must end at 4; commuting tags can produce 6. The reverse order must end at 6.
[1,1] isolates the strictness bug; change only upper_bound to lower_bound in solve().
Floyd-Warshall is correct without negative cycles for all-pairs distances; its stated time and memory fit n<=180, so replacement is unnecessary.
[3,-5,4] has prefix sums 3,-2,2, so the predicate prefix>=2 is true,false,true and binary lifting is invalid.
No input, algorithm, operations, or size variables exist from which correctness or linear cost can be checked.
A query that pushes into shared children writes nodes reachable from old roots, violating version immutability despite correct update path copying.
Each point update can allocate Theta(log U)=Theta(60) nodes, so the node bound is O(q log U), not O(q) when U is a parameter.

conditions: If both operands are 32-bit int and their product exceeds INT_MAX, overflow occurs before assignment.
If an operand is already widened or the product fits, that conclusion does not follow.

evidence.summary: C++ usual arithmetic conversions use operand types, not the destination type; declarations are therefore necessary.
For child i, prefix[i] contains exactly earlier children and suffix[i+1] exactly later children; associativity and the identity make their combination equal the fold excluding i.
